    // `iterations` passes over both joint kinds, distance joints first. The
    // ordering is arbitrary and it matters: Gauss-Seidel converges to the same
    // answer either way, but reaches it along a different path, so a simulation is
    // reproducible only against a fixed order.
    SolveJoints(bodies: Array<SolverBody3D>, distanceJoints: Array<DistanceJoint>,
        ballSocketJoints: Array<BallSocketJoint>, iterations: Integer, stiffness: Number,
        seconds: Number): Array<SolverBody3D>
        => Indices(iterations).Reduce(bodies, (acc, i) =>
            SolveBallSocketJointPass(
                SolveDistanceJointPass(acc, distanceJoints, stiffness, seconds),
                ballSocketJoints, stiffness, seconds));
}
